utterances.text: He wrote the report to me in English, and, frankly, it's a little bit awkward in places. I am just saying that when he makes his -- when he testifies, he will testify in Dutch, and I will have an interpreter here so that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: That's his choice. If he doesn't feel comfortable in English, he can testify in Dutch.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He can write a report in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLER
utterances.text: I don't know that he really considered it a report when he wrote it to me. It came over my E-Mail. But, then, as I told the Court, he went on holiday for three weeks right about that time. So I just went ahead and gave it to the Prosecution as I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Maybe his English is better than Dutch.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLER
utterances.text: Well, I don't know, Your Honour. His English is fine, and I commend him for speaking to me in English, because it certainly made our communications -- I didn't have to have an interpreter, but I believe his choice will be to testify in Dutch.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: We'll let him speak whatever language he wants.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLER
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I suppose these are all the technical areas, I think, that required some observation.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honour, just so I am nailed down, and you know that my last witness is Dr. Gripon, and I have assured the Court that I will be finished before August 1st, I was asking, that since he comes from the United States, if I could get, just like you scheduled Dr. Bellas's testimony for some certain time in the future, I am asking that Dr. Gripon's testimony be scheduled for July 30th. He is my last witness. That will assure the Court, and possibly myself, that we will be completed by then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: It will save some expense also.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: So I would like a date certain for him to appear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. McHenry, I think this suits us.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: We have no objection to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: We'll let you got today before six o'clock, so that you can at least receive your fax.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: My faxes all come in at one and two in the morning, unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You even have paediatricians, a paediatrician as a witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: As a fact witness, not as an expert. Your Honour, I assume that there's about five witnesses on my list that will not be coming to testify. I just gave myself latitude there. There may be four, five or even six witnesses who may not appear that are on this list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I thought that for a paediatrician to testify on behalf of an adult -- that's tracing it back to when he was a baby, is it?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I wanted to bring to the Court's attention, Ms. Boler had said I had scheduled Dr. Gripon for July 29th, if that would make the Court feel any better.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLER
utterances.text: In the motion it says the 29th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: That's all right.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It might be wise, if you find that some of them are not so relevant, to avoid them, because it might cloud what you are really coming out to say. It might create problems for you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I'm afraid that my witness list will be diminished not because of my deciding that they are not relevant, but for other reasons, and that's why I gave myself a little latitude. I believe it will be difficult to get a few of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: As you think fit.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I will, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Because you are in a better position.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I should be. You are right. I will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: There are no restraints on you. There are no restraints on you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You are free. As long as you do not jeopardise your client, you are free.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Well, thank you. I am doing the best to try to give the Court an accurate representation of what I think our Defence case is going to be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Now, I suppose this is your main motion. The other aspects, I don't know which other motion you want to take.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't have any other things before the Court other than, you know, approval to call those expert witnesses. I will have Dr. Gripon's report filed tomorrow. Other than that, all I am asking is that everything that you've just granted me. So I am very satisfied. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You are not likely to work under any constraints.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I see, after a year and a half, Judge Jan knows me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I suppose you will be able to give the Prosecution the report so that they can grant you leave to call Dr. Lammers and Dr. Haeseker. I think --

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLER
utterances.text: Your Honour, did I understand you -- thanks. The night before last -- of course I was sick and not in Court yesterday, so I don't have it before me, but the night before last I did file that with the reports. And, granted, they are short reports, but I believe the testimony will be short as well. So I didn't know if you were telling me that I needed to get a second report or will this one suffice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: If you have a copy of the report, just make a copy of it and give it to them, because that's what you rely upon.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: We received one page of a Lammers report. The other report is in Dutch.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLER
utterances.text: The one page on the hand doctor is in Dutch, and I am in the process of having somebody in our Defence area get that translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: All you need is a translation of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I don't think that will take much longer at all. It's just one page. And part of the page is a picture of a hand, so more like three quarters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Now, there is a motion I saw on my table this morning about all the Defence Counsel suggesting that we should travel to Konjic community and the Celebici premises. Did the Prosecution receive that too?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: We have received it, Your Honour, and our response is, although we do not think it's necessary, or we would have filed it ourselves, we defer to the Court as to whether or not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I thought we have used the model.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: We have the dimensions of the rooms. We even know that one part of it falls on M17 and the main gate is 300 metres away. So why do you want us to go there?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I think it's as if we are already there. Every morning I see this model.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: There are some --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: I think the population was 1200, 1300 people. This is within the premises of that village --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: We know its location, we know the dimensions of the various rooms or hangars or tunnels, we know the dimensions. So why do you want us to visit that place?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Well, I don't believe the Court knows the proximity of the little villages all around.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: We got a very, very large map, what do you call it, ordinance map. You got the whole thing before us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I think there's one witness who says he has a girlfriend in the neighbouring village. Nobody has mentioned about a neighbouring village. No other witness did.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Well, I am not suggesting that the Court can't understand all of this, you know, with the models. The models have been -- there's a few things that are missing on the model that maybe the Court would be able to see if they -- the eye view from building 22 to tunnel 9. There are things that you really can't tell unless you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Got the dimensions here.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: If the Court is satisfied, then of course -- it was just a suggestion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Actually, I have not seen -- noticed any difficulty in appreciating the evidence when you gave it. If I have been having that, there would be anxiety to go and discover these things myself, but all along things have been smooth --

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: You are absolutely right, and I will do my best to make sure that you know that Mr. Delalic's house is first going back into Konjic, et cetera, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You are driving into the place, on the right you get to his house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You didn't get the point which I was trying to make on that day. Why pick on Delalic for a statement? Maybe the house is first, but if Delalic had nothing to do, why ask him? That is the explanation I was trying to get, nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I misunderstood. It was my fault, because I thought that -- I certainly can't respond about Delalic's case. I just thought --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: I was just trying to find out an explanation. Said that we were waved, we stopped, and I really like to make a statement on Celebici, and I just wanted to find out, why pick on him to make that statement?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I understand your question, Your Honour, and it really doesn't have to do with logistics, then, but it was just a suggestion to the Court. And if you feel certainly satisfied that you understand the surrounding area --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: We know that his house is along the river, it is a place which is not accessible to the shelling, to those persons who were doing the shelling. This is a place where a communication centre has been set up. Before that it was being used as a disco. What else do you want us to know about that house?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Well, the disco is still there, Your Honour. There are two separate parts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I don't think it is really necessary for us to --

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: If the Court feels they don't need to, we waive the motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: We are satisfied with what we've heard, and there is no problem about identifying what everyone was saying, because even if you mention the way the detainees are sitting down, there is no reason to reconstruct that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: We have a picture of that. Produce it for us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: These are not things which -- we can visualise these things. So thank you very much for your effort in bringing clarity into the whole exercise, but I think we can do without this one. I think this is all we have for now. So thank you very much for your assistance. We'll be back on Monday at 10.00 in this same Courtroom. Thank you.
